emails.body:
Venlo moves to the new EWM release in Q1 2027, after Rotterdam. We need to fix the cut-over weekend and I see three options: 16 Jan, 30 Jan or 13 Feb 2027.

The plan has four phases: data migration, training, dress rehearsal and the cut-over weekend itself. Each option shifts all four. My gut feeling is that January is tight because of peak season, but I want your view on the outbound volumes before I put a recommendation together.

I would like to decide in a workshop on 5 Nov at 09:00. Jeroen, can you tell me which weeks are critical for Venlo outbound? Mark, you are in copy so you can see where we stand.

January is the problem. The December peak runs into mid-January because of returns and the Q1 promo shipments. Last year we averaged about 2,400 outbound deliveries per day in the first three weeks of January, against roughly 1,600 per day in February.

Also, our temp staff contracts end on 31 Jan, so a go-live on 30 Jan would put the new system on the floor exactly when we lose people. 16 Jan is out for me, because the training would have to happen in December, the busiest weeks.

So 13 Feb is my preference, but please show me what it does to the training slots.

Thanks both. Hanna, can you put the three options side by side with the dates for all four phases? I want to see what a later date costs us. My concern with 13 Feb is that it is close to the end of Q1 and leaves little room if the dress rehearsal fails.

Please also tell me how long the training needs. In Rotterdam I remember it was a point of discussion.

Here is the overview per option. Training is two weeks in all cases, split by shift. Data migration is about four weeks including two test loads.

Option 13 Feb leaves three weeks between the end of training and the cut-over, which is fine for the dress rehearsal and still leaves a fallback slot on 27 Feb. Option 16 Jan puts the training in the December peak, which Jeroen already flagged.

Thanks, that helps. With 13 Feb the training on 18-29 Jan still overlaps with the tail of the January peak, but it is manageable if we train per shift. I have 42 operators who need training, so I would do three groups of 14.

Two questions: what happens if the dress rehearsal on 5-6 Feb goes badly, and how many key users do you need from my side? I can free up people, but not during the same days as the rehearsal.

Three groups of 14 works for me, two sessions per group.

If the rehearsal fails, we hold a go/no-go right after it, on Monday 8 Feb. With a no-go the next slot is the weekend of 27 Feb. That is the reason I would rather not plan the primary date later than 13 Feb.

From Venlo I need four key users. They support the training and are on the floor during the cut-over weekend. Can you send me the names?
Ok, understood on the 27 Feb fallback. I will send you the four key user names by Friday 23 Oct, I just need to check the shift rosters first.

I have read the thread. I will join the workshop on 5 Nov at 09:00 and I expect us to leave with a decision on the date. Hanna, please send me a one-page recommendation by Tuesday 3 Nov, with the risks per option.

My current view is that 13 Feb is the most sensible choice given the peak, as long as the 27 Feb fallback is agreed with Venlo upfront. Jeroen, please check that nothing else in the Venlo calendar conflicts with 13-14 Feb.

Forwarding the lessons learned from the Rotterdam go-live that Ruud Jansen shared with me. Please read it before the workshop on 5 Nov.

The points that matter most for Venlo: 38 of about 4,100 bins had stock differences after migration, the one-day handheld training was too short, and the cut-over took 31 hours instead of the 24 planned. I want to use these in the Venlo plan.

attachment.name: Rotterdam_EWM_lessons_learned.pdf
attachment.text:
Rotterdam EWM go-live - lessons learned

1. Data migration: 38 of about 4,100 bins showed stock differences after the final load. Cause: open transfer orders not closed before the extract. Action: close all open TOs and run a count 2 days before cut-over.
2. Training: one day of handheld (HHT) training was too short. Two days recommended.
3. Cut-over: planned 24 hours, actual 31 hours. Label printer queues had to be reconfigured on the Sunday.
4. Hypercare: 2 weeks with 3 people on the floor was just enough.

emails.body:
Thanks Hanna, useful. Three things from my side for Venlo:

1. We do a stock count in the bins 2 days before the cut-over weekend, and close all open transfer orders first, as Rotterdam advises.
2. I want two days of handheld training, not one. That fits within the two training weeks you planned.
3. I would like hypercare of 3 weeks instead of 2, because we have more operators than Rotterdam.

Can we put these on the agenda for 5 Nov?

42 Venlo operators need training, in three groups of 14 with two sessions per group.
If the dress rehearsal fails, a go/no-go is held on Monday 8 Feb and the fallback slot is the weekend of 27 Feb.
Hanna Schmidt needs four Venlo key users, whose names Jeroen will send by 23 Oct.
